text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Warren Christopher says the time is right for new diplomatic efforts to solve disputes in Cyprus and the Aegean.
- Austrian man living in Cyprus commits suicide.
- Cyprus put pressure on Athens for Gerassimos Arsenis to remain at the Greek ministry of defence.
- The government defence fund will receive 89 million pounds ($193 million) in income this year.
CYPRUS MAIL
- The goverment gives an angry response to remarks by a United Nations envoy praising the Turkish Cypriot side's answer to President Glafcos Clerides demilitarisation proposal.
- Private television channels are to defy rights contract and screen local soccer.
- Police suspect suicide behind Austrian man's plunge.
HARAVGHI
- Internal strife breaks out in (right wing) Disy party over its candidates who will run in December's municipal elections.
- Civil servant dismissed for his alleged involvement in the 1974 coup but subsequently reinstated by the government gets a promotion.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Petroleum companies threaten to stop bringing petroleum products to Cyprus because of liquidity shortage.
- Clothing association wants clarifications on what happened to EU subsidies to help industry.
- Man attempts to murder his girlfriend in Limassol.
SIMERINI
- A dialogue with Turkey could lead to a new Zurich agreement, says outgoing Greek defence minister Arsenis.
- The US is expected to speed up its initiatives on Cyprus and the Aegean.
- Clothing industries appeal to unions : 'Stop asking from us'. ($=0.46 pounds)
